doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Shearing group: guitar predecessors, Bill Clark, McKibbon, vibes, conga
summary: Toots names the members of Shearing's quintet, Dick Garcia before him, Al McKibbon, Joe Roland and Cal Tjader, and later Armando Peraza.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: In Philly, mm-hmm. So Chuck Wayne was the original guitarist. So he’s the one who went in…
Dick Garcia. G-A-R-C-I-A. I wonder if he’s still alive.
And so, who else was in the George Shearing group? How large was it?
Uh… George, of course. Billy Hart for drums. Fantastic drummer. [inaudible]. It feels good, he said, with [Lang?] there.
H-A-R-T. [Billy?] didn’t make a name for himself [inaudible].
So it’s a different… must be a different Billy Hart than the one that…
Yeah. Okay. And who else? So drums, piano, yourself on guitar and harmonica. Bass player, maybe? No?
Oh, so before John Levy took… No, yeah… the other way.
No, that was [wasn’t?] John Levy anymore.
[inaudible/overlapping voices] be Al McKibbon that [date?]. Yeah.
And [inaudible]. Vibraphone was Joe Roland for a while and then Cal Tjader…

Then later on, George added the conga drum. Armando Perazza. There is some fantastic [inaudible] from that [inaudible]. But I don’t know. I’m so crazy [about?] these anecdotes are so precious to me, you know.
Well, I know Armando ‘cause he’s in the Bay area. I live in San Francisco. So please, talk about Armando.
Is he still, he still alive?
He’s still… Yeah, he’s still alive.
Oh, I have a phone number for him. I’ll call him. Okay. Not now. [laughs]
